instruction: The Thunderbird email file `/tmp/shift/shift_email.eml` on the first Linux machine identifies which existing Android Clock alarm is the early fallback that must remain enabled and also provides the reconciliation reference. The `2026-06-12` Morning row in `/tmp/shift/roster.xlsx` on the second Linux machine is authoritative for the actual departure alarm. Read both sources, keep the fallback alarm enabled, add the actual departure alarm from the roster as an enabled alarm, and complete the existing `/tmp/shift/log.json` template on the second Linux machine with the fallback alarm label and time, the actual alarm label and time, and the reconciliation reference.
fixture_notes: The email identifies Reminder 07:30 as the retained fallback, provides the unique reconciliation reference, and deliberately omits the authoritative actual-departure label and time.
The Calc Morning row is the only source of the actual Pickup 08:20 alarm values.
The blank log_template.json defines fallback_alarm, actual_alarm, and reference without leaking any values.
Scoring uses positive presence for both requested alarms and structured coexistence fields rather than old/new replacement semantics.
